quarterly_data.signal: Backlog as of December 31, 2025 was $11.94 billion, a 27.4% increase from $9.38 billion at September 30, 2025 and a 99.3% increase from $5.99 billion at December 31, 2024 (Mechanical 75.6% / Electrical 24.4%). Same-store year-over-year backlog rose $5.59 billion (93.2%), primarily on technology-sector bookings at its Texas modular operation ($1.48 billion), a North Carolina operation ($1.26 billion), an Indiana operation ($901.1 million), a Texas operation ($850.2 million) and its Texas electrical operation ($803.4 million). The company expects to recognize approximately 65-75% of its remaining performance obligations over the next 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $11.94 billion (Dec 31, 2025), +99.3% YoY, +27.4% vs Sep 30, 2025; Texas modular operation +$1.48 billion same-store YoY; 65-75% within 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 revenue increased $2.07 billion, or 29.5%, to $9.10 billion, including 26.1% same-store growth; the 10-K says demand has been especially strong in the technology sector, particularly for data centers. Contract liabilities rose by approximately $971.0 million during 2025, including $910.1 million from billings in excess of costs primarily from the timing of billings on projects within the technology sector.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $9.10 billion (+29.5%; same-store +26.1%); contract liabilities +$971.0 million ($910.1 million from billings in excess of costs, mainly technology sector)
